text:
Ring in the new year across Eastern Oregon
Published 6:53 am Monday, December 22, 2025
EASTERN OREGON — The year is coming to an end and celebrations are planned across Northeastern Oregon to usher in 2026.
BAKER COUNTY
Celebrate the new year early at the Baker library
BAKER CITY — Can’t stay awake until midnight to ring in 2026? Then head to the Baker County Public Library, 2400 Resort St., on Dec. 31 for a special celebration from 10 a.m. to noon.
Celebrate early in Halfway
HALFWAY — The Pine Valley Grange in Halfway will celebrate with an “East Coast New Year’s Eve” on Dec. 31. This family-friendly celebration begins at 5 p.m. with a potluck dinner — table service, punch, coffee and tea will be provided; soda will be available for purchase.
The evening includes cards, games and chatting — join a card game, bring games from home, or just visit with others. This portion is free to attend.
A dance starts at 7 p.m. It costs $5 per person or $20 for a family of four or more. Those gathered will ring in the new year at 9 p.m. with the East Coast and wrap up the dance at 10 p.m.
Celebrate the new year at The Cabyn
BAKER CITY — The Cabyn, 1825 Main St., is hosting a New Year’s Eve party from 9 p.m. to 1 a.m. on Dec. 31 for ages 21 and older.
Music will be provided by DJs chriSTopher, MLay and Ryan Duley. There is no cover charge.
Veterans Club rings in the new year with music
BAKER CITY — The Veterans Memorial Club, 2005 Valley Ave., rings in the new year on Dec. 31 with music by the Baker City All-Stars and the Screeching Eels.
Doors open at 7 p.m., and live music runs from 8 p.m. to midnight.
The Screeching Eels blend metal, rock ‘n’ roll and country. Lead singer Celina Fuzi is a Baker City native who combines her vocals with the talents of bassist/guitarist/vocalist Fredrik Anderson at local venues throughout the year. Joining them on New Year’s Eve will be Baker City musicians Jerry Loft on electric guitar and vocals, Michael Porter on electric guitar and Rex Hubbard, of Sumpter, on drums.
The band will cover songs from such artists as Ozzy Osbourne, Billy Idol, The Doors, David Bowie, The Animals, Eagles, Fleetwood Mac, Jefferson Airplane and The Rolling Stones.
Longtime local favorites The Baker City All-Stars, featuring Anderson, Hubbard, Patrick McWeeney and Donnie Counts, will open the evening with a mix of rock and country favorites from Eric Clapton, Eddie Money, Tom Petty, Temple of the Dog, Dwight Yoakam, Waylon Jennings and Garth Brooks, to name a few.
The club is open to the public and features a large dance floor and full bar. There is no cover charge. Guests must be 21 or older.
Teens invited to celebrate the new year in Baker City
BAKER CITY — Andy Micka wants to welcome 2026 with a record-setting New Year’s Eve party for Baker County teenagers.
The free event takes place in the Family Life Center at the Baker City Nazarene Church, 1250 Hughes Lane. The party runs from 6 p.m. on Dec. 31 to 12:30 a.m. on Jan. 1.
Micka said the party has another purpose in addition to giving teenagers a safe place to have fun on what he calls a “high-risk night.”
When participants sign in at the door — no pre-registration is required — the slip includes a question about whether the teen is at risk of being homeless. Micka said Safe Families for Children can help families who don’t have reliable housing.
Safe Families for Children is the lead sponsor for the New Year’s Eve party, the Nazarene Church supplies the venue, and the church’s youth pastor, Josh Snook, is a major contributor to making the event possible, Micka said.
Jonathan Parsons, the Baker City Police Department’s school resource officer, will serve as DJ for the party. The Baker County Juvenile Department, New Directions Northwest, and the Baker County Safe Communities Coalition are also involved.
Micka said Domino’s Pizza in La Grande donates pizza. Jon France, who oversees the food bank at the Northeast Oregon Compassion Center, also helps to ensure partygoers are well-fed.
Micka said this year’s party theme is based on “Stranger Things,” the popular Netflix series. The final episode of the show’s fifth season debuts on New Year’s Eve.
The party features an escape room based on the show. There will also be a photo booth, a Nerf gun battle upstairs at the Family Life Center, and ’80s-style karaoke. Teens are encouraged to wear costumes with an ’80s theme.
Micka said local residents and businesses donate items for a raffle during the party. All teens receive free raffle tickets, and they can earn more tickets by participating in events.
Parents are welcome to attend the party. Those who plan to go should contact Micka at 541-519-6436 or amicka.nocc.safefamiliesbc@gmail.com.
Micka said the nonprofit’s usual sources of money have diminished this year. People who want to donate or volunteer to help during the party can contact him.
GILLIAM COUNTY
Condon Elks Lodge welcomes Michael Parker
CONDON — Singer-songwriter Michael Parker will strum in the new year on Wednesday, Dec. 31, at 8 p.m. at the Condon Elks Lodge, 117 S. Main St.
Hailing from Kennewick, the singer-songwriter plays acoustic country and Americana. Parker said his musical influences come from “artists who carved out their own niche in country music rather than simply diving headfirst into the mainstream,” including Steve Earle and Roger Miller.
Parker is among a group of regional musicians promoted by Two Wolves Media Group. For more information, search www.twowolvesmediagroup.com.
GRANT COUNTY
New year’s costume party planned in John Day
JOHN DAY — The Bare Bones Bar, 679 W. Main St., will have a New Year’s Eve party starting at 8 p.m. The theme is 1970s and 1980s — costumes are encouraged for cash prizes.
A dinner special will be available from 6-9 p.m. For details, check Facebook or call 541-792-7151.
Ring in the new year at the Elks Lodge
JOHN DAY — The John Day Elks Lodge, 140 NE Dayton St., rings in the new year on Dec. 31 with live music by the Desert Roze Band. This event, for members and guests, begins at 6 p.m. with a dinner of prime rib or salmon. For dinner reservations, call 541-575-1824.
UMATILLA COUNTY
Pilot Rock man to set off city’s first New Year’s Eve fireworks
PILOT ROCK — After training for nearly a year at various fireworks shows, it’s almost time for Zachary Drettwan to host his own.
Drettwan spearheaded the upcoming New Year’s Eve fireworks display for the city of Pilot Rock. The show will start at 6:15 p.m. Dec. 31 and should last about 12 minutes.
For an event initially intended for his family and friends, the show has grown into a community-backed affair with residents donating more than $4,000.
“This town does a lot for everyone else. They do a lot for the community,” Drettwan said. “Why don’t we do something that benefits the town?”
Drettwan said he’s excited for the event because he always misses fireworks on the Fourth of July, but the weather is often too dry, windy or hot to be safe. It took four or five meetings to convince the council to support his event.
Donations have surpassed the minimum goal of $2,000 to reach about $4,500. If any money is left over, Drettwan hopes to put it toward a second annual New Year’s Eve fireworks show.
Thanks to donations, attendees can download the app PyroCast (code SGDE) to play music Drettwan synced to the show. During the show, open the app and connect the phone to a stereo system to hear the synced music.
Though almost anyone on the east side of town will get a good look at the show — which will blast off from near the water tower — Drettwan said the best viewing area will be at Pilot Rock Jr./Sr. High School’s baseball fields. District Superintendent Troy Jerome approved public access to the fields for the fireworks show.
Aaron Harris takes a bite out of New Year’s Eve
HERMISTON — Say farewell to 2025 and ring in 2026 with Heppner native Dog Bite Harris, aka Aaron Harris, during a New Year’s Eve Party on Dec. 31 at Midway Bar & Grill, 1750 N. First St., at 8 p.m.
The singer-songwriter performs a style of music that has been dubbed High Desert Country. Harris brings elements of outlaw country and Americana with a twist.
He got his start in the music industry slinging merch for Bob Wayne. While Harris has ventured out of South Morrow County to live and perform, he eventually returned to his hometown.
Rather than complaining about the lack of live music, he decided to do something about it — launching the inaugural Ruckus in the Boonies in 2014. Featuring country, punk, rockabilly, outlaw country and rock, Ruckus continued through 2018 and then took a five-year hiatus. The festival resumed in 2024.
In addition to nominations for Favorite Regional Acoustic Act and Song of the Year, Harris was selected as a performer during the 2025 Northwest Country Music Association Awards Show, held Nov. 13 in Spokane. A shared consensus from fellow musicians and others in the music industry is that he is talented, passionate and worthy of applause.
“Six strings, a great voice and songwriting that takes the ‘pop’ out of country,” Blake Clayton said in describing Harris’ sound. “He writes and sings about the experiences and feelings of the common folk. His songs put it all on the table, and that, my friends, is what makes real country music.”
“Dog Bite Harris is the kind of singer that doesn’t need to prove his roots to anyone,” Jayke Orvis added. “He’s a road poet that sings about what we all feel.”
The show is presented by Two Wolves Media Group. For more information, visit www.twowolvesmediagroup.com or search Facebook via rebrand.ly/bg4nzrl.
Desert Lanes gets the party rolling
HERMISTON — Get ready to strike into the new year at Desert Lanes Family Fun Center, 1545 N. First St. The family New Year’s Eve event features party packages for up to six people.
The cost is $129.95 and includes 90 minutes of cosmic glow bowling with music, shoe rentals, a large pizza, a pitcher of soda, six $10 arcade cards and party favors.
Sessions run from 3-4:30 p.m., 5-6:30 p.m. and 7-8:30 p.m. on Dec. 31. Reservations are required by calling 541-567-6364.
Resolution Run races into new year in Hermiston
HERMISTON — For more than a decade, an ambitious group of people has hit the ground running (and walking) on New Year’s Day during the Resolution Run.
The non-competitive family-friendly event starts at 10 a.m. on Jan. 1 at Riverfront Park, 500 SW 23rd St. The route encompasses the 3.1-mile Oxbow Trail. However, each person may choose the distance they want to run/walk.
There’s no entry fee, no registration is required and donations aren’t collected for anything. There are no aid stations on the course. However, water will be available at the finish line as well as some high-fives and a photo booth.
This event is sponsored by local runners and walkers who want to encourage people to connect with their neighbors and set personal health and fitness goals for the coming year. Participants are invited to run, trot, skip or walk into the new year. In addition, roller skates, scooters, strollers and well-behaved dogs on leashes are all welcome. The event is not timed.
Check the Resolution Run Facebook page to pre-order branded T-shirts. A limited number will be available for sale at the event.
For more information, search Facebook via rebrand.ly/saeeade. For questions, email timothybeal@gmail.com.
Wildhorse deals in New Year’s Eve fun
MISSION — A full slate of activities are planned to usher in the new year on Dec. 31 at Wildhorse Resort & Casino, located off Interstate 84 Exit 216, about 7 miles east of Pendleton.
Adults 21 and older are invited to play, party and win big from 3-8 p.m. during the Grande Royale Casino Come Alive! in the Rivers Event Center. Entry is free and a cash bar will be available.
Participants will receive $1,000 in FunMoney to play and enter raffles for a chance to win various prizes. Lucky party-goers who are dealt special cards at party tables can enter the Cash Cube to grab and win real money.
Capture memories of your evening by stopping a showgirl making her rounds. Also, stop by the NYE photo booth to create fun snapshots.
Then, from 8:30 p.m. to 12:30 a.m., it’s time to groove and hit the dance floor with Eric Sage’s Hot Hits Show Band. The evening includes party favors and a countdown with confetti cannons.
Also, families and adults can roll into the new year with special New Year’s Eve packages at Quaking Aspens Lanes. Sessions are from 6:30-9 p.m. and 10 p.m. to 12:30 a.m. Reservations are required. The cost for up to six people is $119-$139 and includes shoe rentals, party favors, cosmic lights and countdowns.
And, in the Wildhorse Sports Bar, Bruiser, a rock/pop group, will perform from 8:30 p.m. to midnight. The group also returns Jan. 2-3, from 8 p.m. to midnight. There is no cover charge.
For more information about all the Wildhorse happenings, search www.wildhorseresort.com.
Celebrate the new year at a shootout
PENDLETON — The Blue Mountain Community College Rodeo Boosters is offering a wild way to say goodbye to 2025 with its inaugural New Year’s Eve Blue Mountain Shootout.
The event takes place 7-10 p.m. on Dec. 31 at the Blue Mountain Equine Center, 125 SW 18th St. in Pendleton.
Rebecca Manning, BMCC Rodeo Boosters president, said proceeds from the shootout will benefit the college’s rodeo team.
Events include bull riding, bareback and saddle bronc. Manning said they are expecting 12 contestants per event.
“We’ll crown a winner for each event,” Manning said.
Gold Buckle Rodeo is providing the livestock.
The competition is open to professionals and nonprofessionals.
“You don’t have to be a professional to enter,” Manning said.
She said members of the Blue Mountain rodeo team will be competing and there will also be a barrel man entertaining the crowd.
General admission tickets are $20 plus fees, $10 plus fees for ages 6-12 and those 5 and under get in free. Tickets are available on the event’s Facebook page and at the door.
After the rodeo competition, stick around for the after-event activities. Manning said the shootout is a “family-friendly event with activities for kids.” For more information, visit the BMCC Rodeo Boosters Facebook page.
Music on the Mountain returns to Tollgate
WESTON — Usher in 2026 during Music on the Mountain at Tollgate Crossing Store, 62393 Highway 204, on Dec. 31, starting at 6:30 p.m. All ages are welcome.
Tickets are $55. Entertainment for the evening features Hell’s Belles (all-female AC/DC tribute band), The Piedmont Boys (South Carolina-based honky tonk outlaw country) and the Josh Holland Band (rock/country) from 7 p.m. to midnight.
Fireworks at midnight mark the start of the new year.
Purchase tickets at the store or the Tollgate Crossing Store page on Facebook.
UNION COUNTY
Rock in 2026 at Hot Lake Springs Resort
LA GRANDE — “Rock in” 2026 with a part at Hot Lake Springs Resort, 66172 Highway 203.
Doors open at 7 p.m., and activities run until a champagne toast at midnight (included with tickets, and sponsored by Monkeys on the Run). The celebration wraps up at 1 a.m.
Live music will be provided throughout the evening by The Tattered Hounds, Fading Sage and a live DJ.
Tickets include food and dessert. A no-host bar will stock beer, wine, cider, champagne and cocktails. Also, Monkeys on the Run will have a photo booth, and a raffle runs through the event (must be present to win).
Tickets are $53.65 through hotlakelodge.com. This event is a fundraiser for Friends of Hot Lake, which works to secure grants and donations for preservation projects to restore this historic location. For details, visit nwconservancy.org.
An elegant New Year’s Eve at The Depot
LA GRANDE — For those wishing to usher in the New Year in style, The Depot, 10 Depot St., will open at 4 p.m. on Dec. 31 to celebrate New Year’s Eve and their first anniversary.
Sum People will entertain diners from 7:30-10:30 p.m. with rock, funk, reggae and dance-friendly grooves. For more information, search The Depot on Facebook, visit www.thedepotstreet.com or call 541-306-3377.
Le Bebe Cakes Bakery visits the Old West
LA GRANDE — For those with an adventuresome spirit, Le Bebe Cakes Bakery is bringing back its “Secret Alley Door Speakeasy” on New Year’s Eve, this time with an 1866 Saloon theme. The event begins at 6 p.m. on Dec. 31, and attendees must RSVP to TheSecretAlleyDoorSpeakeasy@gmail.com to receive entry instructions and a required access code.
Western attire is encouraged, and seating is limited. A $10 entrance fee is collected during the RSVP process.
The evening features live music from country duo The Better Halves, with dinner, dessert, and a no-host bar menu available for purchase. The group will toast the New York Ball Drop at 9 p.m., giving attendees the option to continue celebrating downtown or wrap up early.
For more information, check out Le Bebe Cake Bakery’s Facebook page or call 541-963-2253.
HQ goes for the funk this New Year’s Eve
LA GRANDE — HQ, 112 Depot St., is ringing in the New Year with a high-energy celebration featuring Eastern Oregon’s own Good Sax, the two-man funk band known for explosive percussion, funky horn lines, swanky vocals, and irresistible electronic beats.
The beer garden and event space open at 9 p.m., giving guests time to settle in before
Good Sax and special guest musicians take the stage around 10:30 p.m. A suggested donation at the door helps support HQ’s arts and music events, with the option to become a Club Open Stage Member.
For more information on the event or how to become a Club Open Stage Member, visit lagrandehq.com or call 541-612-0551.
La Grande celebrates with a ball drop
LA GRANDE — Capping off the celebrations in downtown La Grande, the New Year’s Eve Ball Drop officially kicks off at 10 p.m., hosted by La Grande Main Street Downtown and sponsored by Monkeys On The Run, at the intersection of Adams Avenue and Depot Street.
The Oregon Festivals & Events Association recognized this festive celebration as one of the best events in Oregon with its “WOW Factor Award,” and La Grande can boast the only New Year’s Eve Ball Drop in the state.
High Country Realty Professionals will provide a warming tent with cookies, coffee and cocoa, and Becky’s Burger Wagon will also be there for folks needing heartier fare. There will be burn barrels set up to warm cold celebrants and a Windows of Downtown La Grande Scavenger Hunt to view the window decorations of downtown merchants and win gift cards and Downtown Coupons.
A countdown to midnight precedes the ball drop, and the celebration will be broadcast live on EOAlive.TV.
For more information, visit the La Grande Main Street Downtown’s Facebook page, check out their website at www.lagrandemainstreet.com or call 541-963-1223.
WALLOWA COUNTY
Start the new year with a Polar Plunge
WALLOWA LAKE — Everyone is invited to start the new year refreshed by jumping in Wallowa Lake on Jan. 1, 2026.
Participants gather around 10 a.m. at the county boat ramp for the annual Beth Gibans Memorial Wallowa Lake Polar Bear Plunge, named for one of the event’s founders, Beth Gibans, who died in 2021 at age 58. It has been going at least since 2007.
